tagline: Former Federal CTO | Engineering & AI Platforms | Technology Leadership
profile: Technology executive and hands-on engineering leader with nearly 20 years in cloud platforms, software development, and AI. Former Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Officer of the Department of Homeland Security, leading more than 150 people, the 50-person AI Corps, and a $10 billion IT portfolio. Today builds and operates production AI platforms and develops the engineers who run them.
about: I believe effective technology leadership requires understanding the entire lifecycle of innovation: identifying the problem, designing the solution, building the technology, earning organizational adoption, and delivering measurable value. My career has let me approach that lifecycle as a software engineer, enterprise architect, federal CTO, AI executive, commercial solution engineer, and senior leader in a growing tech-enabled services small business.

experience.title: Senior Vice President, Solution Engineering
experience.description: Lead solution engineering and all AI technology for a 200-person tech-enabled services small business, combining hands-on engineering with technical strategy and growth.
achievements: Deployed and operate all of the company’s AI technology, from commercial platforms and internal chatbots to AI-assisted development tools and custom automation, at more than 1.5 billion tokens a month with no significant outage.

Architected and built, largely as the sole developer, a shared enterprise AI platform on Amazon EKS with centralized model access and governance controls, on a cluster averaging 190 deployments a month.
Hired, onboarded, and developed a team of 10 LLM, machine learning, data, and full-stack engineers, building each person’s career path in AI engineering, AI operations, or generative AI.
Led company-wide AI upskilling that engaged more than 40% of the workforce, and partnered with program delivery leaders to bring AI and automation to approximately 50% of active projects.

Architected and built an AI platform with multi-source ingestion and hybrid search that automated opportunity discovery, evaluation, and proposal workflows, cutting proposal development time by 60% as the business development pipeline grew 150%.
Supported Amivero’s 2026 acquisition by Xpect Solutions, a NewSpring Holdings platform company, through executive management briefings and technology due diligence.
evidence: Led technology innovation, solution engineering, and AI transformation initiatives, combining hands-on technical leadership with business development, organizational growth, and strategic planning.
Architected and developed secure enterprise AI infrastructure, generative AI chatbots, and reusable data and AI platforms supporting internal operations and federal customer missions.
Developed tailored innovation plans with program delivery leadership, implementing mission-driven AI and automation technologies across approximately 50% of active projects within existing contracts.

Led company-wide AI literacy, upskilling, and reskilling initiatives, engaging more than 40% of the workforce through a gamified program of weekly spy-themed challenges with a leaderboard, and empowering employees to develop AI solutions that improved productivity and operational efficiency.

Architected and developed a proprietary AI-powered growth intelligence platform that automated opportunity discovery, evaluation, and proposal workflows, increasing the business development pipeline by 150% and reducing proposal development time by 60%.

Led technical growth and capture efforts that converted greenfield Data and AI opportunities into contract wins through customer engagement, technical demonstrations and challenges, proposal development, and oral presentations.

Supported Amivero’s successful acquisition by Xpect Solutions, a NewSpring Holdings platform company, in 2026 through executive management briefings and technology due diligence. Executed an AI strategy that strengthened the company’s capabilities and market differentiation.

Deployed and operate all of the company’s AI technology for a 200-person company: commercial platforms, internal chatbots, AI-assisted development tools, and custom automation, at more than 1.5 billion tokens a month with no significant outage in the first year.

Architected and built, largely as the sole developer, a shared enterprise AI platform on Amazon EKS with a single model gateway (LiteLLM to Anthropic Claude on Amazon Bedrock), so every product reaches models through one governed route; the cluster is managed with Argo CD and averages 190 deployments a month across patches, fixes, new features, backend improvements, and new services.

Took two production AI systems in turn from idea to internal pilot in eight weeks and to full operation in three months each, building with AI coding agents (Claude Code), and ran the customer discovery, feedback, training, and intake that brought them into use.

Built that platform as a content-curation and retrieval service: one pipeline ingests SharePoint, CRM, federal opportunity, and web sources, and serves hybrid search with reranking, a Microsoft Teams assistant, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools to AI assistants under each user’s own identity.

Deployed the company’s secure generative AI chat service for staff on open-source software, with single sign-on through Microsoft Entra ID, document-grounded answers using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and tool use through MCP.

Led the agentic case analysis for a security-clearance adjudication system at the Department of Homeland Security, released to production in three months: an orchestration model with parallel specialist sub-agents and tool-calling that batch-analyzes cases against federal adjudicative guidelines before they reach an adjudicator; it has since analyzed thousands of cases.

Evaluated each version of that case analysis against ground-truth historical cases as champion and challenger, measuring true positives, false positives, false negatives, token use, and time to completion in a formal process modeled on NIST practice; the winning version immediately raised the true-positive rate by 30% and cut the false-negative rate by 30%, each relative to the prior version’s results.

Created the design system for the company’s AI case-analysis application, setting common patterns for chat interaction, tool calls and citations, collaboration features, and navigation; a DHS component adopted it for its production adjudication platform.

Built evaluation into the company’s AI systems: citation checks that drop any finding whose quote does not match its source, LLM-as-judge review of generated plans, a synthetic case generator with an evaluation harness, and precision, recall, and F1 threshold sweeps that tuned fraud-ring detection against a ground-truth set.

Built an AI assistant for security-clearance adjudication that combines hybrid retrieval over a vector store with a Neo4j knowledge graph of policy and case, proposing issues, worksheets, and briefs in which every finding cites its source and a person makes the decision.

Built a graph-analytics platform for fraud and identity investigations on Neo4j that scores shared attributes between accounts, detects linked clusters, and explains each link to the investigator, with sensitive identifiers stored only as keyed hashes.
Built internal developer tooling that turns GitHub issues into pull requests using Claude Code agents in isolated worktrees, with secret scanning, protected branches, and no automatic merge.
Migrated the GSA Login.gov program’s CRM from Airtable to Salesforce: about 10,000 records, eight weeks from start to cut-over.
Mentored a machine learning engineer over a year until they took ownership of the company’s AI platforms, working to the organization’s new engineering standards.

Hired, onboarded, and developed a team of 10 LLM, machine learning, data, and full-stack engineers, building each person’s career path in AI engineering, AI operations, or generative AI from their own goals through on-the-job practice, formal training, demonstrated skills, and contributions back to the community.

experience.title: Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Officer
experience.description: Provided technical oversight and organizational leadership, including the management of artificial intelligence initiatives, for a $10B IT portfolio spanning 22 components and offices within the Department of Homeland Security. Led more than 150 people (100 federal employees and 50 contractors) with a $15M budget.
achievements: Helped establish the DHS Office of the Chief AI Officer and led the nationwide recruitment of 50 AI experts from industry, academia, and government, designing the organizational model and setting compensation.
Directly led the DHS AI Corps of 50 AI engineers and product owners and about six engineers in the Chief Technology Officer’s organization.

Developed leaders and talent from within, promoting a project manager and two engineering branch chiefs to Division Directors and creating learning pathways that certified about two dozen employees across the components.
Led development and enterprise deployment of a secure agentic generative AI chatbot, authorized at the FISMA and FedRAMP Moderate level, serving approximately 20,000 DHS personnel.
Ran the department’s enterprise DevOps and collaboration service for more than 13,000 users and more than 300 applications, systems, and projects at over 99% availability.
Developed and implemented department-wide AI governance policies, standards, and workforce training for responsible adoption of generative AI and facial recognition.
Negotiated a department-wide Login.gov enterprise agreement, generating more than $2.5 million in cost avoidance and establishing a unified authentication capability for external-facing services.
evidence: Helped establish the DHS Office of the Chief AI Officer and led a nationwide recruitment initiative that hired 50 AI experts from industry, academia, and government: designed the organizational model, set and approved compensation, ran many of the interviews, and served as second-level supervisor.
Directed enterprise platforms including secure DevSecOps toolchains, generative AI applications, and information-sharing solutions.

Led the engineering teams in that organization directly: the DHS AI Corps of 50 AI engineers and product owners, about 70% of them engineers, and about six engineers in the Chief Technology Officer’s organization.

Organized the office into seven divisions: AI governance, technology governance, the DHS AI Corps, enterprise architecture, engineering, emerging technologies, and business operations, led through two deputies and a director for each division.

Mentored and promoted leaders from within: a project manager who rose to branch chief and then Division Director of AI Governance, and two engineering branch chiefs who became Division Directors of Engineering and of Technology Governance.

Stood up a second side of the organization for AI governance, engineering, and the AI Corps: selected its leaders, led the reorganization and its communication, and resolved conflict and poor performance among existing leaders.

Ran the department’s enterprise DevOps and collaboration service (GitLab, the Atlassian suite, Nexus Repository) supporting CI/CD for more than 13,000 users and more than 300 applications, systems, and projects at multiple service levels; it ran at over 99% availability, with cloud automation managing its environments.

Led the 2024 response to a zero-day vulnerability in the department’s Atlassian Data Center platform, used by 12,000 people: confirmed exposure and every affected server, service, and endpoint with the vendor, tested the patch in non-production (build, smoke, and performance tests), and after a go/no-go decision rolled it out across the cluster with zero downtime.

Absorbed an unplanned 50% increase in charged-back cloud storage costs without raising prices to the platform’s customers: recovered 60% by renegotiating the memorandum of agreement with the peer office that supplied cloud services and used the platform without charge, and 40% by archiving unused projects with their owners and moving older projects to lower-cost storage tiers.
Set the DevOps platform’s pricing model for its customer components each year, charging back the cost of a service used across the department.

Managed the custom-built enterprise architecture platform used by thousands of architects and engineers across the department for the technical reference model, approved software, and the enterprise inventory of systems, products, and software.
Consolidated two support contracts into one, saving 20% by removing duplicate program management, operations, and help desk roles.

The Chief Technology Officer’s organization operationally ran the department’s AI program: the DHS AI Corps, AI policy and governance, DHS Chat, facial recognition technology testing, policy, and reporting, management of the DHS Chief AI Officer Council, and the DHS AI Governance Board.

Developed and implemented the department’s facial recognition technology policy, and led the effort to have every DHS facial recognition system formally tested and validated against NIST and IEC testing requirements, resolving all concerns and issues found; this made DHS one of the most mature organizations in the federal government for safe facial recognition in performance, testing, and governance and compliance.

Created department-wide learning pathways in AI engineering, secure software development, and human-centered design, certifying about two dozen employees from across the components in multiple cohorts.

focus.title: AI Engineering & Innovation
focus.body: I build AI systems that solve real problems. From generative AI and intelligent automation to secure enterprise platforms and responsible governance, I help organizations move beyond experimentation and make emerging technology practical, secure, and valuable.

focus.title: Technology Leadership & Transformation
focus.body: I’ve led engineering teams and enterprise transformation across government and industry. Successful transformation takes strong teams, a clear strategy, an understanding of organizational culture, and the ability to turn ambitious goals into executable plans.

focus.title: Strategic Growth & Business Development
focus.body: I connect technology with business strategy through federal sales, technical capture, customer engagement, and differentiated solutions. My experience includes opportunity shaping, executive management briefings, and M&A technology due diligence.

focus.title: Hands-On Engineering & Product Development
focus.body: I’ve never stopped being an engineer. I design architectures, write code, and build applications, exploring distributed systems, cloud-native infrastructure, AI orchestration, automation, and data platforms. Staying hands-on is part of being an effective technology leader.

journey: My career began in software engineering, driven by curiosity about how technology works and how it can make complicated things simpler. That curiosity grew into a career spanning federal technology leadership, enterprise modernization, commercial solution engineering, artificial intelligence, and business growth.

I served as CTO at ICE, worked in commercial solution engineering at Salesforce, and returned to DHS as Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Officer. During my federal career, I modernized large-scale technology environments, established enterprise engineering capabilities, and advanced responsible AI adoption across complex government missions.

At Amivero, I combined hands-on engineering with technical strategy and business development: building secure AI capabilities, accelerating adoption across customer programs, and improving operational efficiency. I also participated in executive management briefings and technology due diligence supporting the company’s acquisition by Xpect Solutions in 2026.
Throughout these experiences, one thing has remained constant: I enjoy building things, solving difficult problems, and working with talented people to create something meaningful.

beyond: Technology has always been both my profession and my hobby. Interactive games, whether video, board, or role-play, have always been an outlet for me to express creativity, think critically, and have fun. As a technologist and creator, I want to work with teams to create new stories, experiences, and challenges for people the way the games of my life have for me. I’m a lifelong gamer and a huge fan of role-playing and strategy games, from MMOs to turn-based and real-time strategy, and I’m building my first game in Unreal Engine 5. I also enjoy Dungeons & Dragons, 3D printing, home automation, electronics, and experimenting with development tools. Whether I’m building an AI application or a home project, I’m usually learning something new.

approach.title: Strategy Is Important. Execution Is Everything.
approach.body: A great technology strategy should be ambitious enough to change what’s possible and practical enough to implement. That requires understanding the technology, the organization, and the people who depend on the outcome. Sometimes the greatest improvements come from simplifying processes, reusing proven capabilities, or removing unnecessary complexity.

approach.title: Build Capabilities, Not Just Projects
approach.body: A successful project solves an immediate problem. A well-designed platform can help an organization solve an entire class of problems. I look for opportunities to create reusable AI infrastructure, development platforms, automation, and shared services, while being deliberate about where standardization creates value beyond the original use case.

approach.title: Make Innovation Accessible
approach.body: Transformation succeeds when people across an organization can participate. AI literacy, workforce development, and practical education help the people closest to a problem apply technology to their work. My role is to create the environment, tools, and guardrails that empower them to innovate responsibly.

approach.title: Connect Technology to Outcomes
approach.body: Complexity is never the objective. What matters is whether a solution improves customer experience, reduces operational friction, accelerates delivery, or creates new opportunities. Effective technology leaders move between vision, architecture, engineering, organizational change, and measurable results.

shortBio: Dave Larrimore is a technology executive, AI engineer, and former federal Chief Technology Officer with nearly 20 years of experience driving enterprise modernization, technology innovation, and business growth. He has served in senior leadership roles at DHS and ICE, overseeing large-scale technology portfolios and advancing enterprise cloud and AI capabilities. As Senior Vice President of Solution Engineering at Amivero, he combined hands-on AI engineering with technology strategy and business development. His work included enterprise AI platforms and proprietary automation that increased the business development pipeline by 150% and reduced proposal development time by 60%. He also supported executive management briefings and technology due diligence during Amivero’s acquisition by Xpect Solutions in 2026. Dave remains an active technologist, building software and exploring AI, product engineering, and organizational transformation.
